To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the alternative plans differ in terms of commitment of stakeholders.

(1) the most important determinant for commitment is the perceived probability of the alternative management plans to be successful, and (2) the most important factors that determine the perceived probability of success are the economic consequences for the stakeholders and the biological consequences for the fish stocks.

(a) The management plans were evaluated as having different levels of commitment by stakeholders; (b) The commitment was based on stakeholders' views of the plans' effects on the Baltic salmon stocks and their own livelihoods; (c) The plans' effects on stakeholders' views were based on the stakeholders' own values and on the values of the stakeholders' reference groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the analysis of expert knowledge in fisheries management, and the application of Bayesian nets to fisheries management.
the implementation and management uncertainty of the Baltic salmon fishery.
the question how to use expert knowledge in the design and implementation of long-term management plans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alternative plans were not very different from one another in terms of the commitment of the stakeholder groups to them.
the alternative plans are not equally well suited for the management of salmon stocks in the Baltic Sea.
commitment of different groups to the management options is dependent of the groups' interests, which in turn is dependent of the management options.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of Bayesian networks is a promising approach to formalizing expert knowledge in fisheries.
we were able to show how a qualitative analysis could be coupled with a probabilistic Bayesian network in analysing expert's knowledge related to alternative management plans in terms commitment.

the use of Bayesian nets is a promising approach for the management planning process, and that it is possible to use Bayesian nets to formalize expert knowledge in order to analyze the effects of alternative management plans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Bayesian nets can provide an efficient way for integrating different kinds of data and knowledge in a transparent manner.
it is possible to combine qualitative and quantitative analysis in a way that is transparent and allows for the use of the results in the management process.
the Bayesian network approach is a promising tool for integrating different types of information and for visualising the complex interrelations between the variables.
